posts.author: IcySnowflake
posts.body:
First time posting, apologies if this is in the wrong channel.
Recently I've been hand-drawing all of my enemies for my game on an A4 document, but for RMMV it's way too big to even fit on the troops screen. Sizing down them in a separate image editor makes it appear blurry and lowers the quality by loads.
I feel like there's a better way to do this to keep the image quality whilst still fitting it for the editor, but I've tried things like AI downscaling and multiple image editors like Canva, Krita and Pixlr with no such luck. Is there a plugin that could help? Or a method I don't know of? If so it would be highly beneficial if someone could provide some advice or link to help me out.
Note: I have tried drawing them at the smaller sizes but it just doesn't look as good as it does at the A4 size.

posts.author: Neutrality
posts.body:
Just to be clear, what's your game's default resolution? I think it would also be helpful if you could post some screenshots of the enemies, usually this type of scenario depends on the kind of art style they have.
I believe some editors include a function known as Anti-Aliasing that smoothens out the image, which may not work for the drawings you've made since if they're pixelated they become blurry to see.

posts.author: SGHarlekin
posts.body: An A4.. Document? Sounds odd. Generally speaking, if done right, dowsizing isn't really losing any quality unless you're doing it wrong. You'd have to downsize it by a whole number (Like half size for example) If you're not doing that, it's gonna get blurry.

posts.body:
Thank you for the replies!
At the moment, I'm running it through the default Battle Test window to avoid potentially having to redo a lot of the artwork in the case that I end up having to draw them at a smaller resolution. Bare in mind I'm not a brilliant artist, but here's one of the enemies:

Here's the original rat enemy and the downsized rat enemy side by side in the Battle Test window:

posts.author: ATT_Turan
posts.body:
SGHarlekin said:
dowsizing isn't really losing any quality unless you're doing it wrong.
Click to expand...
That's not entirely the case, because when you're making something smaller you necessarily have fewer pixels to display the details in the original drawing.
That being said, the OP's picture really doesn't have enough detail to be seeing much quality loss from being made smaller.
Personally,
@IcySnowflake
, I suggest you're doing this backward. You shouldn't just draw stuff and try to slap it into your game; you should know how big you want something to be in your game first, whether that's a 48x48 map tile or whatever size your rat battler should be to look good on the battle screen.
Then you use GIMP or whatever else to make a canvas of that size, zoom in as necessary, and draw there.
